summary: Clarifies and relaxes the IANA registration rules for MIKEY, the Multimedia Internet KEYing protocol. It updates several earlier MIKEY RFCs and replaces RFC 4909.

eli5.summary: This is a rulebook update about how new items get added to a list kept for a key-exchange protocol used with audio and video, making the rules clearer and a bit easier to follow.

questions: what does ietf review or iesg approval mean
what is specification required in iana
subtitle: Loosens the sign-up rules for the MIKEY key-management protocol's IANA registries, so new values need less ceremony.

tldr.problem: MIKEY's registries mostly required "IETF Review" for new values, which was unnecessarily strict for some namespaces and left no room for special cases.
tldr.mechanism: Most namespaces now accept "IETF Review or IESG Approval", several others need only "Specification Required", and a few value ranges are stated explicitly.
tldr.outcome: Allocation is easier and an Independent Stream RFC can suffice for some registries. It obsoletes RFC 4909 and updates RFCs 3830, 4563, 5410 and 6043.

facts.label: S type, Key Data Type, KV Type

today: RFC 6309 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted. It obsoletes RFC 4909 and updates RFC 3830, RFC 4563, RFC 5410 and RFC 6043.

sections.title: Why the Rules Were Relaxed
sections.content:
RFC 6309 relaxes the IANA rules for Multimedia Internet KEYing (MIKEY), defined in RFC 3830. Most MIKEY namespaces are split into two ranges: "IETF Review" (earlier called "IETF Consensus") and "Reserved for Private Use".

The rationale is that sometimes it makes sense to grant an allocation under special circumstances, and that time has shown the old requirement to be unnecessarily strict for some namespaces. The RFC gives an example: an experimental protocol extension could deserve a new payload type, as long as enough types remain and the MIKEY community is happy with it.
sections.eli5: The old rule was like needing the whole school to vote on every new club rule. Some changes are small, so a lighter process was added.

sections.title: IETF Review or IESG Approval
sections.content:
For a long list of namespaces from RFC 3830, the requirement changes from "IETF Review" to "IETF Review or IESG Approval". This lets the IESG consider a request even when it does not meet the default rule. The RFC still encourages IETF Review when there is doubt about whether a new allocation is needed.

The affected namespaces include data type, Next payload, PRF func, CS ID map type, Encr alg, MAC alg, DH-Group, S type, TS type, ID Type, Cert Type, Hash func, SRTP Type, SRTP encr alg, SRTP auth alg, SRTP PRF, FEC order, Key Data Type and KV Type.

New values for the version field and the C envelope key cache indicator field stay with plain "IETF Review".
sections.eli5: For many lists, the group of top reviewers can now say yes to a special case, even if the usual path was not followed.

sections.title: Specification Required Registries
sections.content:
Some registries drop to "Specification Required": Prot type, Error no and General Extension Type from RFC 3830, KEY ID Type from RFC 4563, and OMA BCAST Data Subtype from RFC 5410. For these, a stable specification is enough.

The RFC notes that an RFC published through the Independent Stream at the RFC Editor is sufficient for some registries, and does not force an IETF evaluation of an extension for which there is no general demand.

Four namespaces from RFC 6043 already used "Specification Required" and keep it: TS Role, ID Role, RAND Role and Ticket Type. Their rules are re-specified here, and this RFC now defines their IANA requirements.
sections.eli5: For some lists, you just need to write down clearly what your new item means. A stable written description is enough.

sections.title: Clarified Value Ranges
sections.content:
The IANA considerations of RFC 3830 did not say which values were valid for some namespaces. This RFC states them.

C Envelope Key Cache Indicator
Valid values 0 - 3.
S type, Key Data Type, KV Type
Valid values 0 - 15 for each.
sections.eli5: The lists did not say how long they could be. Now the notes say exactly which numbers can be used.

sections.title: What Changes in Earlier RFCs
sections.content:
Relative to RFC 3830, a number of namespaces now have the "IETF Review or IESG Approval" requirement and some have "Specification Required". The KEY ID Type namespace of RFC 4563 now has "Specification Required".

RFC 5410 obsoleted RFC 4909 but did not define the IANA rules itself. From now on, RFC 6309 defines the IANA requirements for the OMA BCAST Data Subtype namespace. For RFC 6043 there are no changes, only a restatement for completeness.
sections.eli5: Older rulebooks are corrected in a few places. This one is now the place to look for the rules on some lists.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The specification does not change the security properties of MIKEY. However, when new values are introduced without IETF consensus, care needs to be taken to make sure that possible security concerns about the new values are still addressed.
sections.eli5: Making it easier to add things means someone still has to check that the new things are safe.
